answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by pricing identity itself: each agent locks a refundable stake before its votes count, and duplicates split that stake, so clones add no influence. Before activation, an agent proves liveness with small real work - answering a whisper probe, describing a random marble sample, tracing a verification ledge - which honest machines pass cheaply but spam farms cannot profit from. Each forged persona costs locked funds, work fees, and slashing risk on collusion, making sybil attacks strictly costlier than honest participation.
